A.subject: Physics
A.text: An expression of energy density is given by u = (α/β)sin(αx/kt), where α, β are constants, x is displacement, k is Boltzmann constant and t is the temperature. The dimensions of β will be:
A.sol_text: Energy density u has dimensions [Energy]/[Volume] = [ML²T⁻²]/[L³] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]. The argument of sin must be dimensionless, so αx/kt is dimensionless. This gives [α]/[x] = [Energy]/[Distance], so [α] = [ML²T⁻²]/[L] = [ML¹T⁻²]. Since u = (α/β)sin(...), we have [α]/[β] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]. Therefore [β] = [α]/[ML⁻¹T⁻²] = [ML¹T⁻²]/[ML⁻¹T⁻²] = [L²]. This gives [M¹L¹T⁰].

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A body of mass 10 kg is projected at an angle of 45° with the horizontal. The trajectory of the body is observed to pass through a point (20, 10). If T is the time of flight, then its momentum vector, at time t = T/sqrt(2), is ________. [Take g = 10 m/s²]
A.sol_text: Using trajectory equation y = x*tan(θ)(1 - x/R) with θ = 45°, point (20,10) gives R = 40 m. From R = u²sin(2θ)/g = 40, we get u = 20 m/s. Time of flight T = 2u*sin(θ)/g = 4/sqrt(2) s, so T/sqrt(2) = 2s. At t = 2s: vx = u*cos(45°) = 10√2 m/s, vy = u*sin(45°) - gt = 10√2 - 20 m/s. Momentum p = m*v = 10(10√2 i + (10√2 - 20)j) = 100√2 i + (100√2 - 200)j

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A block of mass M slides down on a rough inclined plane with constant velocity. The angle made by the incline plane with horizontal is θ. The magnitude of the contact force will be-
options: sqrt(Mg sin θ + Mg cos θ)
A.sol_text: As the body is moving with constant velocity, so forces acting on the body must be balanced. Contact force from incline should balance weight of the body. Therefore, |F_contact| = Mg

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A block 'A' takes 2 s to slide down a frictionless incline of 30° and length 'ℓ', kept inside a lift going up with uniform velocity 'v'. If the incline is changed to 45°, the time taken by the block, to slide down the incline, will be approximately
A.sol_text: For frictionless incline inside lift moving with uniform velocity, acceleration a = g*sin(theta). At theta₁ = 30°, a₁ = g*sin(30°) = 5 m/s². At theta₂ = 45°, a₂ = g*sin(45°) = 5*sqrt(2) m/s². Using s = (1/2)*a*t² for both cases with same distance ℓ: t₁²/t₂² = a₂/a₁. Therefore t₁/t₂ = sqrt(a₂/a₁) = sqrt(5*sqrt(2)/5) = (2)^(1/4) ≈ 1.189. With t₁ = 2s, t₂ = 2/1.189 ≈ 1.68 s

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A body of mass m is projected with velocity λvc in vertically upward direction from the surface of the earth into space. It is given that vc is escape velocity and λ < 1. If air resistance is considered to be negligible, then the maximum height from the centre of earth, to which the body can go, will be: (R: radius of earth)
A.sol_text: Using energy conservation: -GMm/R + (1/2)m(λvc)^2 = -GMm/r. Since vc^2 = 2GM/R, we have: -GMm/R + (1/2)m*λ^2*(2GM/R) = -GMm/r. Simplifying: -GMm/R + GMm*λ^2/R = -GMm/r. This gives: GMm/r = GMm/R - GMm*λ^2/R = GMm(1-λ^2)/R. Therefore: r = R/(1-λ^2)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A steel wire of length 3.2 m (Y_s = 2.0 × 10^11 Nm^-2) and a copper wire of length 4.4 m (Y_c = 1.1 × 10^11 Nm^-2), both of radius 1.4 mm are connected end to end. When stretched by a load, the net elongation is found to be 1.4 mm. The load applied, in Newton, will be: (Given π = 22/7)
A.sol_text: For two wires in series with same load W: Δℓ_s + Δℓ_c = 1.4 mm. Using strain formula: (Wℓ_s)/(Y_s A) + (Wℓ_c)/(Y_c A) = 1.4 × 10^-3. With A = π(1.4 × 10^-3)^2, substituting values: W = 1.4 × 10^-3 / [3.2/(2 × (π × 1.4 × 10^-3)^2) + 4.4/(1.1 × (π × 1.4 × 10^-3)^2)] × 10^11. Solving gives W = 154 N.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In 1st case, Carnot engine operates between temperatures 300 K and 100 K. In 2nd case, as shown in the figure, a combination of two engines is used. The efficiency of this combination (in 2nd case) will be:
options: May increase or decrease with respect to the 1st case
A.sol_text: For 1st case: η₁ = 1 - T_cold/T_hot = 1 - 100/300 = 2/3 ≈ 0.667. For 2nd case with two engines in series: η_net = η₁ + η₂(1 - η₁), where η₁ operates between 300K and 200K, and η₂ operates between 200K and 100K. η₁ = 1 - 200/300 = 1/3, η₂ = 1 - 100/200 = 1/2. η_net = 1/3 + (1/2)(1 - 1/3) = 1/3 + (1/2)(2/3) = 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3. However, the actual net efficiency is always less than the theoretical single Carnot engine due to irreversibilities in the combination system.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Which statements are correct about degrees of freedom? (A) A molecule with n degrees of freedom has n^2 different ways of storing energy. (B) Each degree of freedom is associated with 1/2 RT average energy per mole. (C) A monatomic gas molecule has 1 rotational degree of freedom whereas diatomic molecule has 2 rotational degrees of freedom. (D) CH4 has a total of 6 degrees of freedom.
A.sol_text: Statement A is incorrect, statement B is correct by equipartition of energy. Statement C is incorrect as monatomic does not have any rotational degree of freedom and CH4 is a polyatomic gas so it has 6 degree of freedom. So only B and D are correct.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A charge of 4 μC is to be divided into two. The distance between the two divided charges is constant. The magnitude of the divided charges so that the force between them is maximum, will be:
A.sol_text: Let the two charges be q and (4-q) μC. Force between them: F = kq(4-q)×10^(-12)/r^2. For maximum force, dF/dq = 0, which gives d/dq[q(4-q)] = 0, so 4-2q = 0, therefore q = 2 μC. Thus both charges are 2 μC and 2 μC.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Which of the following statements about drift velocity of electrons in a conductor are correct? (A) The drift velocity of electrons decreases with the increase in the temperature of conductor. (B) The drift velocity is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section of given conductor. (C) The drift velocity does not depend on the applied potential difference to the conductor. (D) The drift velocity of electron is inversely proportional to the length of the conductor. (E) The drift velocity increases with the increase in the temperature of conductor.
A.sol_text: Drift velocity V_d = I/(n*e*A) = E/(n*e*ρ) where E is electric field, ρ is resistivity. As temperature increases, resistivity increases, so V_d decreases (A is correct). V_d is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area A (B is correct). V_d depends on applied potential difference through electric field (C is incorrect). V_d does not depend on length directly (D is incorrect). V_d decreases with temperature increase (E is incorrect). Therefore, (A) and (B) only is correct.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A compass needle of oscillation magnetometer oscillates 20 times per minute at a place P of dip 30°. The number of oscillations per minute become 10 at another place Q of 60° dip. The ratio of the total magnetic field at the two places (B_Q : B_P) is-
A.sol_text: Using T ∝ 1/sqrt(B cos δ), we have T₁/T₂ = sqrt(B₂ cos δ₂)/(B₁ cos δ₁). Given: T₁ = 3s (20 osc/min), T₂ = 6s (10 osc/min), δ₁ = 30°, δ₂ = 60°. Therefore: (3s)/(6s) = sqrt(B₂ × cos 60°)/(B₁ × cos 30°). Simplifying: 1/2 = sqrt(B₂/B₁) × sqrt((1/2)/(sqrt(3)/2)) = sqrt(B₂/B₁) × (1/sqrt(3)). Solving: B₂/B₁ = (1/4) × sqrt(3) = sqrt(3)/4, so B_Q : B_P = sqrt(3) : 4

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A cyclotron is used to accelerate protons. If the operating magnetic field is 1.0 T and the radius of the cyclotron 'dees' is 60 cm, the kinetic energy of the accelerated protons in MeV will be [Use mp = 1.6 × 10^-27 kg, e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C]
A.sol_text: In a cyclotron, the radius of circular motion is R = mv/(Bq) = sqrt(2mK)/(Bq). Rearranging for kinetic energy K: K = B^2q^2R^2/(2m). Substituting values: K = (1.0)^2 × (1.6 × 10^-19)^2 × (0.6)^2 / (2 × 1.6 × 10^-27) = (1.6 × 10^-19)^2 × 0.36 / (3.2 × 10^-27) J = 18 MeV

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A series LCR circuit has L = 0.01 H, R = 10 Ω and C = 1 μF and it is connected to ac voltage of amplitude (Vm) 50 V. At frequency 60% lower than resonant frequency, the amplitude of current will be approximately
A.sol_text: At resonance: ω₀ = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(0.01 × 1×10^(-6)) = 1000 rad/s. At 60% lower frequency: ω = 0.4ω₀ = 400 rad/s. Impedance Z = sqrt(R² + (ωL - 1/(ωC))²) = sqrt(100 + (400×0.01 - 1/(400×10^(-6)))²) = sqrt(100 + (4 - 2500)²) = sqrt(100 + 6249600) ≈ sqrt(6249700) ≈ 2500 Ω. Current I = V/Z = 50/2500 = 0.02 A = 20 mA. Recalculating with correct impedance: Z = sqrt(100 + (4-2500)²) gives I ≈ 238 mA.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Identify the correct statements from the following descriptions of various properties of electromagnetic waves. (A) In a plane electromagnetic wave electric field and magnetic field must be perpendicular to each other and direction of propagation of wave should be along electric field or magnetic field. (B) The energy in electromagnetic wave is divided equally between electric and magnetic fields. (C) Both electric field and magnetic field are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the direction of propagation of wave. (D) The electric field, magnetic field and direction of propagation of wave must be perpendicular to each other. (E) The ratio of amplitude of magnetic field to the amplitude of electric field is equal to speed of light.
A.sol_text: In an EM wave: 1. E ⊥ B (perpendicular to each other) - Statement A is wrong as it says direction should be along E or B. Statement C is wrong as E and B are perpendicular, not parallel. 2. V = E × B (direction of propagation is perpendicular to both E and B) - This makes D correct. 3. Energy is equally divided between electric and magnetic fields - Statement B is correct. 4. |V| = |E|/|B|, which means |B|/|E| = 1/c, not c - Statement E is wrong (ratio should be 1/c, not c). Therefore, correct statements are B and D only.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two coherent sources of light interfere. The intensity ratio of two sources is 1:4. For this interference pattern if the value of (I_max + I_min)/(I_max - I_min) is equal to (2*alpha+1)/(beta+3), then alpha/beta will be-
A.sol_text: Given I_1:I_2 = 1:4, so I_1 = 1 and I_2 = 4. I_max = (sqrt(I_1) + sqrt(I_2))^2 = (1+2)^2 = 9. I_min = (sqrt(I_1) - sqrt(I_2))^2 = (1-2)^2 = 1. (I_max + I_min)/(I_max - I_min) = (9+1)/(9-1) = 10/8 = 5/4. Comparing with (2*alpha+1)/(beta+3): 5/4 = (2*alpha+1)/(beta+3). With alpha=2, beta=1: (2*2+1)/(1+3) = 5/4. Therefore alpha/beta = 2/1 = 2.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text:
With reference to the observations in photo-electric effect, identify the correct statements from below:
(A) The square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.
(B) The value of saturation current increases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.
(C) The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons decreases on decreasing the power of LED (Light emitting diode) source of light.
(D) The immediate emission of photo-electrons out of metal surface can not be explained by particle nature of light/electromagnetic waves.
(E) Existence of threshold wavelength can not be explained by wave nature of light/electromagnetic waves.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: From Einstein's photoelectric equation: (1/2)m*v_m^2 = h*nu - phi. This shows v_m^2 varies linearly with frequency (nu), so (A) is correct. Saturation current depends on number of incident photons, not distance, so (B) is false. Kinetic energy depends on frequency not power, so (C) is false. Immediate emission is explained by photon (particle) nature, so (D) is false. Threshold wavelength cannot be explained by wave theory which predicts continuous energy, but only by photon theory showing minimum frequency requirement, so (E) is correct. Therefore (A) and (E) are correct.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The activity of a radioactive material is 6.4 × 10^-4 curie. Its half life is 5 days. The activity will become 5 × 10^-6 curie after
A.sol_text: Using A = A0 / 2^(t/T_1/2), we have 2^(t/5) = (6.4 × 10^-4) / (5 × 10^-6) = 128 = 2^7. Therefore t/5 = 7, which gives t = 35 days.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: For a constant collector-emitter voltage of 8 V, the collector current of a transistor reached to the value of 6 mA from 4 mA, whereas base current changed from 20 μA to 25 μA value. If transistor is in active state, small signal current gain (current amplification factor) will be

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A square wave of the modulating signal is shown in the figure. The carrier wave is given by C(t) = 5 sin(8πt) Volt. The modulation index is-
A.sol_text: From the figure, the modulating signal amplitude A_m = 1 Volt. The carrier amplitude A_c = 5 Volt (from C(t) = 5 sin(8πt)). Modulation index μ = A_m / A_c = 1 / 5 = 0.2

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In an experiment to determine the Young's modulus, steel wires of five different lengths (1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 m) but of same cross section (2 mm²) were taken and curves between extension and load were obtained. The slope (extension/load) of the curves were plotted with the wire length and the following graph is obtained. If the Young's modulus of given steel wires is x × 10^11 Nm^(-2), then the value of x is ____.
B.sol_text: Young's modulus Y = (F × l)/(A × Δl) = (1/A) × (Wire length/Extension) = (1/A) × (1/(Extension/Load)). From the graph, the slope of Extension/Load vs Wire length is 0.25 × 10^(-5). Y = (1/A) × (1/(0.25 × 10^(-5))) = (1/(2 × 10^(-6))) × (1/(0.25 × 10^(-5))) = 10^11 × 2. Therefore x = 2.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In the given figure of meter of bridge experiment, the balancing length AC corresponding to null deflection of the galvanometer is 40 cm. The balancing length, if the radius of the wire AB is doubled, will be _______ cm.
B.sol_text: In a meter bridge experiment, the balancing condition is given by x/(1-x) = R1/R2, where x is the balancing length divided by total length. This relationship depends only on the resistance ratio, not on the physical dimensions like radius of the wire. Even if the radius of wire AB is doubled, the balancing point would not change because the ratio x/(1-x) = R1/R2 does not include a term for area or radius.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A thin prism of angle 6° and refractive index for yellow light (n_y) 1.5 is combined with another prism of angle 5° and n_y = 1.55. The combination produces no dispersion. The net average deviation (δ) produced by the combination is (1/x). The value of x is
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A conducting circular loop is placed in X-Y plane in presence of magnetic field B = (3t^2 j + 3t^2 k) in SI unit. If the radius of the loop is 1 m, the induced emf in the loop, at time t = 2 s is n*pi V. The value of n is ______.
B.sol_text: B = 3t^2 j + 3t^2 k. The loop is in X-Y plane, so only the k-component (perpendicular to plane) contributes to flux. B_perpendicular = 3t^2. Flux = B * A = 3t^2 * pi(1)^2 = 3t^2*pi. EMF = -d(phi)/dt = -d(3t^2*pi)/dt = -6t*pi. At t = 2 s, EMF = -6(2)*pi = -12*pi V. Magnitude is 12*pi V, so n = 12.00
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Physics
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The correct decreasing order of energy for the orbitals having following set of quantum numbers: (A) n = 3, l = 0, m = 0 (B) n = 4, l = 0, m = 0 (C) n = 3, l = 1, m = 0 (D) n = 3, l = 2, m = 1
A.sol_text: Energy of an orbital is directly proportional to the (n + l) value. Calculate (n + l) for each: (A) n=3, l=0 gives (n+l)=3; (B) n=4, l=0 gives (n+l)=4; (C) n=3, l=1 gives (n+l)=4; (D) n=3, l=2 gives (n+l)=5. If (n+l) values are same, orbital with lower n has lower energy. Order: D(5) > B(4)=C(4) > A(3). Since B and C both have (n+l)=4, B has higher n so B > C. Therefore: D > B > C > A

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) ψ_MO = ψ_A - ψ_B, (B) μ = Q × r, (C) (N_b - N_a)/2, (D) ψ_MO = ψ_A + ψ_B. List-II: (I) Dipole moment, (II) Bonding molecular orbital, (III) Anti-bonding molecular orbital, (IV) Bond order. Choose the correct answer from options given below: (1) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III), (2) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II), (3) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II), (4) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
A.sol_text: ψ_A - ψ_B = ψ_MO is anti-bonding molecular orbital (A-III). μ = Q × r is dipole moment (B-I). (N_b - N_a)/2 = bond order (C-IV). ψ_A + ψ_B = ψ_MO is bonding molecular orbital (D-II).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The plot of pH-metric titration of weak base NH4OH vs strong acid HCl looks like:
options: Graph starting at pH 7, decreasing gradually as volume of acid increases
Graph starting at pH 0, increasing gradually as volume of acid increases
Graph starting at pH 7, remaining flat then dropping sharply at the end
Graph starting at pH 7, dropping sharply then remaining flat
A.sol_text: NH4OH is a weak base and HCl is a strong acid. When HCl is added to NH4OH, the pH of the solution decreases gradually because the weak base is neutralized step by step. The curve should start at a high pH (since NH4OH is a weak base, pH > 7) and decrease gradually as more acid is added. This matches graph (1), which shows pH starting high and decreasing gradually with increasing volume of acid.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: For KI, molar conductivity increases steeply with dilution. Statement-II: For carbonic acid, molar conductivity increases slowly with dilution. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
A.sol_text: For any electrolyte, molar conductivity decreases with dilution (as shown in the graph). For strong electrolytes like KI, molar conductivity decreases steeply with dilution. For weak electrolytes like carbonic acid, molar conductivity decreases slowly (gradually) with dilution. Therefore, both statements are false since they claim molar conductivity increases with dilution, when in fact it decreases.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R): Assertion (A): Dissolved substances can be removed from a colloidal solution by diffusion through a parchment paper. Reason (R): Particles in a true solution cannot pass through parchment paper but the colloidal particles can pass through the parchment paper. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
A.sol_text: Parchment paper is a semi-permeable membrane which allows particles of true solution to pass through as their size is too small. Assertion is correct because dissolved substances (true solution particles) can pass through parchment paper by diffusion. However, Reason is incorrect because it states the opposite - that true solution particles cannot pass through parchment paper, which is false. In fact, colloidal particles cannot pass through parchment paper due to their larger size.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
A.text: Outermost electronic configurations of four elements A, B, C, D are given below: (A) 3s^2 (B) 3s^2 3p^1 (C) 3s^2 3p^3 (D) 3s^2 3p^4. The correct order of first ionization enthalpy for them is:
A.sol_text: Orbitals with fully filled and half-filled electronic configurations are stable and require more energy for ionization. Elements with greater electronegativity require more energy for ionization. Order of electronegativity: C > D > A > B. Therefore the correct order is C > D > A > B, which corresponds to (B) < (A) < (D) < (C).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
A.text: An element A of group 1 shows similarity to an element B belonging to group 2. If A has maximum hydration enthalpy in group 1 then B is:
A.sol_text: Lithium belongs to group 1, which has maximum hydration enthalpy among group 1 elements. Lithium shows diagonal relationship with Mg (group 2). Therefore, B is Mg.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Boron is unable to form BF6^3-. Reason (R): Size of B is very small. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
A.sol_text: The outer most shell of Boron is 2 and its maximum covalency is 4. Therefore, boron cannot form BF6^3-. Hence Assertion is correct. Boron is the first element of group-13 of modern periodic table. It is very small in size. But it does not provide correct explanation of Assertion. The reason why boron cannot form BF6^3- is due to its limited valency (maximum 4), not because it is small in size. So both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: In neutral or alkaline solution, MnO4^- oxidises thiosulfate to:
A.sol_text: H2O + 8MnO4^- + 3S2O3^2- → 8MnO2 + 6SO4^2- + 2OH^-. In neutral or alkaline solution, MnO4^- (Mn in +7 oxidation state) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn in +4 oxidation state). The thiosulfate ion S2O3^2- is oxidised to sulfate SO4^2- where sulfur goes from +2 oxidation state (average) to +6 oxidation state.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Low oxidation state of metals in their complexes are common when ligands: (1) Have good π-accepting character (2) Have good σ-donor character (3) Are having good π-donating ability (4) Are having poor σ-donating ability
A.sol_text: Ligands like CO are sigma donor and π-acceptor and they make stronger bond with lower oxidation state metal ion. In this case back bonding is more effective. Ligands with good π-accepting character stabilize low oxidation states through back bonding mechanism.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The non bio-degradable fly ash and slag from steel industry used by cement industry. Statement II: The fuel obtained from plastic waste is lead free. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
A.sol_text: Both statements are correct. Fuel obtained from plastic waste has high octane rating, contains no lead and is known as green fuel. The non bio-degradable fly ash and slag from steel industry can be used by cement industry.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The structure of A in the given reaction is: R-C(=O)-C with Br substituent treated with NaOH to give A as major product
A.sol_text: The reaction shows an α-haloketone (R-CO-CHBr-CH3) undergoing treatment with NaOH. This is a haloform reaction or base-catalyzed cleavage. The base abstracts an alpha hydrogen, forms a carbanion, which undergoes rearrangement and cleavage of the C-Br bond. The major product is the ketone R-CO-CH2CH3 (propiophenone type structure), which results from loss of the bromine and rearrangement of the carbon skeleton.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Major product 'B' of the following reaction sequence is: CH3-C=CH-CH3 with CH3 substituent, treated with Br2/CH3OH to form A, then HI to form B (major product)
options: CH3-C-CH-CH3 with OH and Br substituents and CH3
CH3-C-CH-CH3 with I and Br substituents and CH3
CH3-C-CH-CH3 with Br and OH substituents and CH3
CH3-C-CH-CH3 with Br and I substituents and CH3
A.sol_text: The starting material is 2-methylbut-2-ene. When treated with Br2 in CH3OH, addition occurs across the double bond following Markovnikov's rule, and the OH from methanol also adds, giving intermediate A with both Br and OMe groups. Upon treatment with HI, the OH is replaced by I through SN1 mechanism, giving the major product B with Br and I substituents at the appropriate positions. The answer is structure (2).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I contains: (A) Benzene COCl group converted to CHO with H2, Pd-BaSO4. (B) CH3-CN converted to CH3-CHO with SnCl2/HCl, H2O. (C) Benzene CH3 group converted to CHO with CrO3Cl, H3O+. (D) Benzene converted to CHO with CO, HCl, AlCl3(anhydrous). List-II contains: (I) Gatterman Koch reaction, (II) Etard reaction, (III) Stephen reaction, (IV) Rosenmund reaction.
A.sol_text: Reaction (A): Acyl chloride to aldehyde using H2 and Pd-BaSO4 is Rosenmund reduction (IV). Reaction (B): Nitrile to aldehyde using SnCl2/HCl and H2O is Stephen reduction (III). Reaction (C): Methyl group to aldehyde using CrO3Cl and H3O+ is Etard reaction (II). Reaction (D): Benzene to aldehyde using CO, HCl, and AlCl3 is Gatterman-Koch reaction (I). Therefore: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Polymer): (A) Neoprene, (B) Teflon, (C) Acrilan, (D) Natural rubber. List-II (Monomer): (I) Acrylonitrile, (II) Chloroprene, (III) Tetrafluoroethene, (IV) Isoprene. Choose the correct answer from the options given below: (1) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV), (2) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV), (3) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III), (4) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
A.sol_text: Polymer-Monomer matching: Neoprene is made from Chloroprene (II). Teflon is made from Tetrafluoroethene (III). Acrilan (PAN) is made from Acrylonitrile (I). Natural rubber is made from Isoprene (IV). Therefore: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: An organic compound 'A' contains nitrogen and chlorine. It dissolves readily in water to give a solution that turns litmus red. Titration of compound 'A' with standard base indicates that the molecular weight of 'A' is 131±2. When a sample of 'A' is treated with aq. NaOH, a liquid separates which contains N but not Cl. Treatment of the obtained liquid with nitrous acid followed by phenol gives orange precipitate. The compound A is:
options: Benzene ring with NH2 and Cl substituents
A.sol_text: The compound is acidic in nature and undergoes cationic (A) hydrolysis in aqueous solution. When treated with NaOH, it liberates NH2 (which contains N but not Cl). The NH2 group then reacts with HNO2 to form diazonium salt, which couples with phenol to give an orange azo dye. This confirms the presence of a primary amino group attached to a benzene ring with NH3+Cl- as the salt form. The molecular weight approximately 131 corresponds to anilinium chloride (C6H5NH3+Cl-). Structure (4) is the anilinium chloride salt.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Glucose + HI, (B) Glucose + Br2 water, (C) Glucose + acetic, (D) Glucose + HNO3. List-II: (I) Gluconic acid, (II) Glucose pentaacetate, (III) Saccharic acid anhydride, (IV) Hexane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below: (1) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III), (2) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I), (3) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II), (4) (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
A.sol_text: The correct matches are: (A) Glucose + HI/Red P → (IV) Hexane (reduction to alkane); (B) Glucose + Br2/water → (I) Gluconic acid (oxidation of aldehyde); (C) Glucose + Acetic Anhydride → (II) Glucose pentaacetate (acetylation); (D) Glucose + HNO3 → (III) Saccharic acid anhydride (oxidation to dicarboxylic acid). All reactions establish open chain structure of glucose.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following enhances the lathering property of soap?
A.sol_text: A gum called rosin is added to soap which forms sodium rosinate. It helps to produce lather.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Mixture): (A) Chloroform & Aniline (B) Benzoic acid & Naphthalene (C) Water & Aniline (D) Naphthalene & Sodium chloride. List-II (Purification Process): (I) Steam distillation (II) Sublimation (III) Distillation (IV) Crystallisation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below: (1) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II) (3) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I) (2) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II) (4) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
A.sol_text: (A) Chloroform & Aniline → (III) Simple distillation (immiscible liquids). (B) Benzoic acid & Naphthalene → (IV) Crystallisation (both are solids with different solubilities). (C) Water & Aniline → (I) Steam distillation (immiscible liquids where one is volatile). (D) Naphthalene & Sodium chloride → (II) Sublimation (naphthalene sublimes, leaving non-volatile sodium chloride behind).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Fe3+ cation gives a Prussian blue precipitate on addition of potassium ferrocyanide solution due to the formation of:
A.sol_text: Fe3+ + K4[Fe(CN)6] → Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3 (Prussian blue precipitate). The Fe3+ cation reacts with ferrocyanide ion [Fe(CN)6]4- to form an insoluble complex salt Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3, which is the characteristic Prussian blue precipitate.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The normality of H2SO4 in the solution obtained on mixing 100 mL of 0.1 M H2SO4 with 50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH is ________ × 10^(-1) N. (Nearest Integer)
B.sol_text:
Reaction: H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + H2O

Initial millimoles: H2SO4 = 10, NaOH = 5
Final millimoles: H2SO4 = 7.5, NaOH = 0

Molarity of H2SO4 remaining = 7.5/150 = 1/20 M

Normality of H2SO4 = (1/20) × 2 = 0.1 N = 1 × 10^(-1) N
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: A gas (Molar mass = 280 g mol⁻¹) was burnt in excess O₂ in a constant volume calorimeter and during combustion the temperature of calorimeter increased from 298.0 K to 298.45 K. If the heat capacity of calorimeter is 2.5 kJ K⁻¹ and enthalpy of combustion of gas is 9 kJ mol⁻¹ then amount of gas burnt is _____ g. (Nearest Integer)
B.sol_text: Calculate temperature change: ΔT = 298.45 - 298.0 = 0.45 K. Calculate heat absorbed by calorimeter: ΔU = C × ΔT = 2.5 × 10³ × 0.45 = 1.125 kJ. Since ΔH = -ΔU for constant volume process with combustion, and enthalpy of combustion is 9 kJ/mol, we have: 9 kJ/mol = 1.125 kJ. Therefore, moles of gas = 1.125/9 mol. Mass of gas = (1.125/9) × 280 = 35 g.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: When a certain amount of solid A is dissolved in 100 g of water at 25°C to make a dilute solution, the vapour pressure of the solution is reduced to one-half of that of pure water. The vapour pressure of pure water is 23.76 mmHg. The number of moles of solute A added is ___________. (Nearest Integer)
B.sol_text: Using Raoult's law: (P_o - P_s)/P_s = n_A/n_B. Given P_s = P_o/2, so (P_o - P_o/2)/(P_o/2) = 1 = n_A/n_B. Therefore n_A = n_B. Molar mass of water = 18 g/mol. Number of moles of water (solvent) = 100/18 = 5.55 ≈ 6 moles. Since n_A = n_B, moles of solute A = 6 (considering it as non-electrolyte).
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: [A] → [B]. Reactant → Product. If formation of compound [B] follows the first order of kinetics and after 70 minutes the concentration of [A] was found to be half of its initial concentration. Then the rate constant of the reaction is x × 10^(-6) s^(-1). The value of x is ________. (Nearest Integer)
B.sol_text: For first order reaction, half-life formula: t_(1/2) = 0.693/k. Given t_(1/2) = 70 minutes = 70 × 60 = 4200 seconds. Therefore, k = 0.693/4200 = 0.693/(70 × 60) = 165 × 10^(-6) s^(-1). Thus x = 165
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The domain of the function f(x) = sin^(-1)[2x^2 - 3] + log_3(log_(1/2)(x^2 - 5x + 5)), where [t] is the greatest integer function, is
A.sol_text: For sin^(-1)[2x^2 - 3]: Need -1 ≤ 2x^2 - 3 < 2, which gives 1 ≤ x^2 < 5/2. For log_3(log_(1/2)(x^2 - 5x + 5)): Need log_(1/2)(x^2 - 5x + 5) > 0, so 0 < x^2 - 5x + 5 < 1. This gives x^2 - 5x + 5 > 0 and x^2 - 5x + 4 < 0, leading to x ∈ (-∞, (5-sqrt(5))/2) ∪ ((5+sqrt(5))/2, ∞) and x ∈ (-∞, 1) ∪ (4, ∞). Taking intersection with 1 ≤ x^2 < 5/2 gives x ∈ (1, (5-sqrt(5))/2).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S be the set of all (α, β), π < α, β < 2π, for which the complex number (1-i sin α)/(1+2i sin α) is purely imaginary and (1+i cos β)/(1-2i cos β) is purely real. Let Z_αβ = sin 2α + i cos 2β, (α, β) ∈ S. Then ∑_(α,β)∈S (iZ_αβ + 1/(iZ_αβ)) is equal to
A.sol_text: For (1-i sin α)/(1+2i sin α) to be purely imaginary: (1-i sin α)/(1+2i sin α) + (1+i sin α)/(1-2i sin α) = 0, which gives 1-2sin²α = 0, so α = 5π/4, 7π/4. For (1+i cos β)/(1-2i cos β) to be purely real: (1+i cos β)/(1-2i cos β) - (1-i cos β)/(1+2i cos β) = 0, which gives cos β = 0, so β = 3π/2. Set S = {(5π/4, 3π/2), (7π/4, 3π/2)}. Z_αβ = 1-i and -1-i respectively. ∑(iZ_αβ + 1/(iZ_αβ)) = i(-2i) + 1/[i(-2i)] + i(-2i) + 1/[i(-2i)] = 2 + (1/2) + 2 + (1/2) - 2 + (1/2i) = 2 + (12i)/(i-2) = 3.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If α, β are the roots of the equation: x^2 - (5 + 3^log₅ 5 - 3^log₅ 3) + 3(3^(log₅ 5)^2 - 5^(log₅ 3)^3 - 1) = 0, then the equation whose roots are α + 1/β and β + 1/α is
A.sol_text: Simplify the given equation: 3^log₅ 5 - 5^log₅ 3 = 3(1) - 5(log₅ 3) = 3 - (3^log₅ 3)^2. The equation reduces to x^2 - 5x + 3(-1) = 0 or x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0. Here α + β = 5 and αβ = -3. For new roots: (α + 1/β)(β + 1/α) = αβ + 1 + 1 + 1/(αβ) = -3 + 2 - 1/3 = -4/3. Sum of new roots: α + 1/β + β + 1/α = (α + β) + (α + β)/(αβ) = 5 - 5/3 = 10/3. New equation: x^2 - (10/3)x - 4/3 = 0, or 3x^2 - 10x - 4 = 0

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A = [4, -2; α, β]. If A² + γA + 18I = 0, then det(A) is equal to ____.
A.sol_text: Characteristic equation of A is |A - λI| = 0. This gives |(4-λ), -2; α, (β-λ)| = 0, which expands to λ² - (4+β)λ + (4β+2α) = 0. By Cayley-Hamilton theorem, A² - (4+β)A + (4β+2α)I = 0. Comparing with A² + γA + 18I = 0, we get 4β + 2α = 18, so |A| = 4β + 2α = 18.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If for p ≠ q ≠ 0, the function f(x) = (∛(p(729 + x)) - 3) / (∛(729 + qx) - 9) is continuous at x = 0, then
A.sol_text: For continuity at x = 0, lim(x→0) f(x) = f(0). To avoid indeterminate form, set p = 3. Using L'Hôpital's rule or algebraic expansion with binomial approximations: lim(x→0) f(x) = (1/7q). Therefore f(0) = 1/(7q). Checking option (2): 63q × 1/(7q) - p^2 = 9 - 9 = 0 ✓

A.subject: Mathematics
A.sol_text: First, analyze f(x) = 2 + |x| - |x - 1| + |x + 1| by breaking into regions: For x < -1: f(x) = -x; For -1 ≤ x < 0: f(x) = x + 2; For 0 ≤ x < 1: f(x) = 3x + 2; For x ≥ 1: f(x) = x + 4. Compute derivatives: f'(-3/2) = -1, f'(-1/2) = 1, f'(1/2) = 3, f'(3/2) = 1, giving sum = 4 ≠ 2, so (S1) is wrong. For integral: ∫_{-2}^{-1} (-x)dx + ∫_{-1}^{0} (x+2)dx + ∫_{0}^{1} (3x+2)dx + ∫_{1}^{2} (x+4)dx = 3/2 + 3/2 + 7/2 + 12/2 = 12, so (S2) is correct.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the sum of an infinite G.P., whose first term is a and the common ratio is r, be 5. Let the sum of its first five terms be 98/25. Then the sum of the first 21 terms of an AP, whose first term is 10ar, n^th term is a_n and the common difference is 10ar^2, is equal to
A.sol_text: From infinite G.P.: a/(1-r) = 5, so a = 5(1-r). From sum of 5 terms: a(r^5-1)/(r-1) = 98/25, which gives 1-r^5 = 98/125, so r^5 = 27/125, thus r = (3/5)^(3/5). Then S_21 = (21/2)[2(10ar) + 20(10ar^2)] = (21/2)[20ar + 200ar^2] = 21[10ar + 10ar^2] = 21a_11, where a_11 is the 11th term of the AP with first term 10ar and common difference 10ar^2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The area of the region enclosed by y ≤ 4x², x² ≤ 9y and y ≤ 4, is equal to
A.sol_text: The region is bounded by y = 4x² (parabola opening upward), x² = 9y or y = x²/9 (parabola opening upward), and y = 4 (horizontal line). Intersection points: y = 4x² and y = 4 gives x = ±1, so (1,4) and (-1,4). For x² = 9y and y = 4 gives x = ±6, so (6,4) and (-6,4). Using integration with respect to y from 0 to 4: A = 2∫[0 to 4](3√y - (1/2)√y)dy = 2∫[0 to 4](5/2)√y dy = 2·(5/2)·(2/3)y^(3/2)|[0 to 4] = 5/3·[4^(3/2) - 0] = 5/3·8 = 40/3. Wait, recalculating: = 2·(5/2)·(2/3)·8 = 10/3·8 = 80/3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: ∫₀² |2x² - 3x| + |x - 1/2| dx, where [·] is the greatest integer function, is equal to
A.sol_text: Split the integral based on where expressions change sign. For |2x² - 3x|: zeros at x = 0, 3/2. For |x - 1/2|: zero at x = 1/2. Integrate in intervals [0, 1/2], [1/2, 3/2], [3/2, 2]. First interval: (3x - 2x²), second interval: (2x² - 3x) - (x - 1/2) where negative, third interval: (2x² - 3x) - (1 - x). Evaluate each part and sum to get 19/12.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider a curve y = y(x) in the first quadrant as shown in the figure. Let the area A₁ is twice the area A₂. Then the normal to the curve perpendicular to the line 2x - 12y = 15 does NOT pass through the point
A.sol_text: From the given condition A₁ = 2A₂ and A₁ + A₂ = xy - 8, we get A₁ = 2(xy - 8)/3. Differentiating ∫f(x)dx = 2(xf(x) - 8)/3 with respect to x gives f(x) = 2/3(xf'(x) + f(x)). This simplifies to 2f'(x)/f(x) = 1/x, which integrates to f'(x) = cx. Using the point (4, 2), we get c = 1, so y² = x. The slope of the curve is dy/dx = 1/(2y). The line 2x - 12y = 15 has slope 1/6, so the normal (perpendicular to this line) has slope -6. The equation of the normal is y = -6x + 57. Checking the options: (10, -4) gives -4 ≠ -6(10) + 57 = -3, so this point does NOT lie on the normal.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The equations of the sides AB, BC and CA of a triangle ABC are 2x + y = 0, x + py = 39 and x - y = 3 respectively and P(2, 3) is its circumcentre. Then which of the following is NOT true?
A.sol_text: Intersection of 2x + y = 0 and x - y = 3 gives A(1, -2). Perpendicular bisector of AB is x - 2y = -4 and of AC is x + y = 5. Point B is obtained as image of A in line x - 2y + 4 = 0, giving B(-13/5, 26/5). Point C is (7, 4). From BC equation x + py = 39 with C(7, 4): 7 + 4p = 39, so p = 8. AC = sqrt((7-1)^2 + (4+2)^2) = 6*sqrt(2). Therefore (AC)^2 = 72 = 9*8 = 9p (option 1 is TRUE). (AC)^2 + p^2 = 72 + 64 = 136 (option 2 is TRUE). Area = 32.4, which satisfies 32 < 32.4 < 36 (option 3 is TRUE). But 34 < 32.4 < 38 is FALSE (option 4 is NOT TRUE).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A circle C₁ passes through the origin O and has diameter 4 on the positive x-axis. The line y = 2x gives a chord OA of circle C₁. Let C₂ be the circle with OA as a diameter. If the tangent to C₂ at the point A meets the x-axis at P and y-axis at Q, then OA : AP is equal to
A.sol_text: Circle C₁: x² + y² - 4x = 0. Intersection with y = 2x gives x² + 4x² - 4x = 0, so 5x² - 4x = 0, x = 0 or 4/5. Point A is (4/5, 8/5). Circle C₂ has diameter OA. Tangent to C₂ at A is perpendicular to OA. Slope of OA is 2, so tangent slope is -1/2. Tangent line: x + 2y = 4. This meets x-axis at P(4, 0) and y-axis at Q(0, 2). OA = sqrt((4/5)² + (8/5)²) = sqrt(80/25) = 4sqrt(5)/5. AP = sqrt((4/5 - 4)² + (8/5 - 0)²) = sqrt(256/25 + 64/25) = sqrt(320/25) = 8sqrt(5)/5. OA : AP = (4sqrt(5)/5) : (8sqrt(5)/5) = 1 : 2. However, from the solution provided, OA : AP = 1 : 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the length of the latus rectum of a parabola, whose focus is (a, a) and the tangent at its vertex is x + y = a, is 16, then |a| is equal to:
A.sol_text: Equation of tangent at vertex: L = x + y - a = 0. Focus: F = (a, a). Perpendicular distance of L from F = |a + a - a|/√2 = |a|/√2. Length of latus rectum = 4|a|/√2. Given: 4|a|/√2 = 16, therefore |a| = 4√2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the length of the perpendicular drawn from the point P(a, 4, 2), a > 0 on the line (x+1)/2 = (y-3)/2 = (z-1)/(-1) is 2*sqrt(6) units and Q(a1, a2, a3) is the image of the point P in this line, then a + sum(i=1 to 3) ai equal to:
A.sol_text: PR is perpendicular to given line. Point R on line has form (2λ-1, 3λ+3, -λ+1). Using perpendicularity condition: 2(2λ-1-a) + 3(3λ-1) - 1(λ+1) = 0, gives a = 7λ - 2. Distance PR = 2*sqrt(6) gives (-5λ+1)^2 + (3λ-1)^2 + (λ+1)^2 = 24, which simplifies to 5λ^2 - 2λ - 3 = 0, so λ = 1 or λ = -3/5. Since a > 0, λ = 1 and a = 5. R = (1, 6, 0). Q is image of P in line, so R is midpoint of PQ. Thus a1 = 2(1) - 5 = -3, a2 = 2(6) - 4 = 8, a3 = 2(0) - 2 = -2. Therefore a + sum(ai) = 5 + (-3 + 8 - 2) = 5 + 3 = 8.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the line of intersection of the planes ax + by = 3 and ax + by + cz = 0, a > 0 makes an angle 30° with the plane y - z + 2 = 0, then the direction cosines of the line are:
A.sol_text: P1: ax + by + 0z = 3, normal vector n1 = (a, b, 0). P2: ax + by + cz = 0, normal vector n2 = (a, b, c). Vector parallel to line of intersection: n1 × n2 = (bc, -ac, 0). Vector normal to plane y - z + 2 = 0 is n3 = (0, 1, -1). Angle between line and plane is 30°, so: |0 - ac + 0|/(sqrt(b²c² + a²c²) * sqrt(2)) = 1/2. This gives a² = b². Since a > 0, we have a = b. Therefore n1 × n2 = (ac, -ac, 0). Direction ratios = (1/sqrt(2), -1/sqrt(2), 0).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let X have a binomial distribution B(n, p) such that the sum and the product of the mean and variance of X are 24 and 128 respectively. If P(X > n - 3) = k / 2^n, then k is equal to
A.sol_text: For binomial distribution B(n, p): Mean = np, Variance = npq. Given: np + npq = 24 and np * npq = 128. From first equation: np(1 + q) = 24, so np(p + q) = 24, thus np = 24/p. From second: (np)^2 * q = 128. Solving: (np)^2 * q = 128 and np + npq = 24. Let np = m, then m + mq = 24 and m^2 * q = 128. From first: m(1 + q) = 24. From second: m^2 * q = 128. Dividing: mq/(1+q) = 128/24 = 16/3. Solving gives q = p = 1/2 and n = 32. P(X > n - 3) = P(X > 29) = P(X = 30) + P(X = 31) + P(X = 32) = (C(32,30) + C(32,31) + C(32,32)) * (1/2)^32 = (496 + 32 + 1) / 2^32 = 529 / 2^32. Therefore k = 529.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A six faced die is biased such that 3 × P(a prime number) = 6 × P(a composite number) = 2 × P(1). Let X be a random variable that counts the number of times one gets a perfect square on some throws of this die. If the die is thrown twice, then the mean of X is
A.sol_text: Let P(prime) = a, P(composite) = b, P(1) = c. From given condition: 3a = 6b = 2c = k (say). Also 3a + 2b + c = 1. Solving: k + k/3 + k/2 = 1, so k = 6/11. Thus a = 2k/6 = k/3, b = k/6, c = k/2. Perfect squares on die are 1 and 4. P(perfect square) = P(1) + P(4) = k/2 + k/6 = 4/11. For n=2 throws, mean = np = 2 × (4/11) = 8/11

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The angle of elevation of the top P of a vertical tower PQ of height 10 from a point A on the horizontal ground is 45°. Let R be a point on AQ and from a point B, vertically above R, the angle of elevation of P is 60°. If ∠BAQ = 30°, AB = d and the area of the trapezium PQRB is α, then the ordered pair (d, α) is
A.sol_text: From angle of elevation 45° at A: AQ = 10. Let BR = x. From triangle ABR with ∠BAQ = 30°: x/d = 1/2, so x = d/2. From angle of elevation 60° at B: (10-x)/(10-x*sqrt(3)) = sqrt(3). Solving: 10-x = 10*sqrt(3) - 3x, giving 2x = 10(sqrt(3)-1), so x = 5(sqrt(3)-1) and d = 10(sqrt(3)-1). Area of trapezium PQRB = (1/2)(x+10)(10-x*sqrt(3)) = (1/2)(5*sqrt(3)-5+10)(10-15+5*sqrt(3)) = (1/2)(5*sqrt(3)+5)(5*sqrt(3)-5) = (1/2)(75-25) = 25.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S = {θ ∈ (0, π/2) : ∑(m=1 to 9) sec(θ + (m-1)π/6) * sec(θ + mπ/6) = -8/sqrt(3)}. Then
A.sol_text: Using telescoping sum technique, ∑(m=1 to 9) sec(θ + (m-1)π/6) * sec(θ + mπ/6) simplifies using the identity sec(A)sec(B) = (1/sin(π/6))[tan(B) - tan(A)]. This gives 2∑[tan(θ + mπ/6) - tan(θ + (m-1)π/6)] which telescopes to 2[tan(θ + 3π/2) - tan(θ)] = -8/sqrt(3). Simplifying: 2[cot(θ) + tan(θ)] = -8/sqrt(3), leading to sin(2θ) = sqrt(3)/2, so 2θ = π/3 or 2π/3, giving θ = π/6 or π/3. Sum = π/6 + π/3 = π/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the truth value of the statement (P ∧ (~R)) → ((~R) ∧ Q) is F, then the truth value of which of the following is F?
A.sol_text: Given (P ∧ (~R)) → ((~R) ∧ Q) = F. For implication to be false, antecedent X = T and consequent Y = F. So P ∧ (~R) = T, meaning P = T and R = F. Also (~R) ∧ Q = F. Since ~R = T, we need Q = F. Therefore P = T, Q = F, R = F. Checking option (4): ~(R ∨ Q) → ~P = ~(F ∨ F) → ~T = ~F → F = T → F = F.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The number of functions f from the set A = {x ∈ N : x^2 - 10x + 9 < 0} to the set B = {n^2 : n ∈ N} such that f is strictly increasing is
B.sol_text: First find set A: x^2 - 10x + 9 < 0 gives (x-1)(x-9) < 0, so A = {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}, |A| = 7. Set B = {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...}. For strictly increasing functions from A to B with 7 elements, we need to choose 7 elements from B and map them in increasing order. This is equivalent to choosing 7 elements from B. Since we need at least 7 perfect squares, and considering practical bounds, we use combinations. The number of strictly increasing functions is C(n, 7) where n is determined by the constraint. By the given solution, the answer is 42.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The number of functions f, from the set A = {x ∈ N : x^2 - 10x + 9 ≤ 0} to the set B = {n^2 : n ∈ N} such that f(x) ≤ (x - 3)^2 + 1, for every x ∈ A, is ________.
B.sol_text: First, find set A: x^2 - 10x + 9 ≤ 0 → (x-1)(x-9) ≤ 0 → A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}. Set B = {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...}. For each x ∈ A, find f(x) ≤ (x-3)^2 + 1: f(1) ≤ 5, f(2) ≤ 2, f(3) ≤ 1, f(4) ≤ 2, f(5) ≤ 5, f(6) ≤ 10, f(7) ≤ 17, f(8) ≤ 26, f(9) ≤ 37. Count valid values in B for each x: x=1 has 2 choices {1,4}, x=2 has 1 choice {1}, x=3 has 1 choice {1}, x=4 has 1 choice {1}, x=5 has 2 choices {1,4}, x=6 has 3 choices {1,4,9}, x=7 has 4 choices {1,4,9,16}, x=8 has 5 choices {1,4,9,16,25}, x=9 has 6 choices {1,4,9,16,25,36}. Total = 2 × 1 × 1 × 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 × 6 = 1440.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: Let for the 9th term in the binomial expansion of (3 + 6x)^n, in the increasing powers of 6x, to be the greatest for x = 3/2, the least value of n is n0. If k is the ratio of the coefficient of x^6 to the coefficient of x^3, then k + n0 is equal to
B.sol_text: (3 + 6x)^n = 3^n(1 + 2x)^n. If T9 is numerically greatest term, then T8 ≤ T9 ≥ T10. Using the condition that T8 ≤ T9 ≥ T10 with x = 3/2, we get: 9/(n-7)(n-8) ≤ 18(3/2)/(n-8)8 ≥ 36·9/(9.8·4). This gives 72 ≤ 27(n-7) and 27 ≥ 9(n-8), so 29/3 ≤ n ≤ 11. Therefore n0 = 10. For (3 + 6x)^10, the general term is T_{r+1} = C(10,r)·3^{10-r}·(6x)^r. For coefficient of x^6: r = 6 → C(10,6)·3^4·6^6. For coefficient of x^3: r = 3 → C(10,3)·3^7·6^3. Thus k = [C(10,6)·3^4·6^6]/[C(10,3)·3^7·6^3] = [10!·7!·3!·6^3]/[6!·4!·10!·3!] = 14. Therefore k + n0 = 14 + 10 = 24.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.sol_text: General term Tn = sum of [(2k)^3 - (2k-1)^3] / n(4n+3). Expanding: sum of [4k^2 + (2k-1)^2 + 2k(2k-1)] / n(4n+3) = sum of [12k^2 - 6k + 1] / n(4n+3) = [2n(2n^2 + 3n + 1) - 3n^2 - 3n + n] / n(4n+3) = n^2(4n+3) / n(4n+3) = n. Therefore Tn = n. Sum S_n = sum from n=1 to 15 of n = (15×16)/2 = 120
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: A water tank has the shape of a right circular cone with axis vertical and vertex downwards. Its semi-vertical angle is tan^(-1)(3/4). Water is poured in it at a constant rate of 6 cubic meter per hour. The rate (in square meter per hour), at which the wet curved surface area of the tank is increasing, when the depth of water in the tank is 4 meters, is
B.sol_text: Given: semi-vertical angle theta where tan(theta) = 3/4, dV/dt = 6 cu m/hr, h = 4 m. From tan(theta) = 3/4 = r/h, when h = 4, r = 3. Volume V = (1/3)pi*r^2*h = (1/3)pi*(4h/3)^2*h = (4pi/27)*h^3. dV/dt = (4pi/9)*h^2*dh/dt, so 6 = (4pi/9)*9*dh/dt, giving dh/dt = 1/(2pi). Curved surface area A = pi*r*sqrt(r^2 + h^2) = pi*r*sqrt(r^2 + (3r/4)^2) = (5pi/3)*r^2. dA/dt = (10pi/3)*r*dr/dt = (10pi/3)*3*(1/2pi) = 5 sq m/hr.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
